title: Sixteen-bit view of the code points in Hello算法
summary: Align English and Chinese characters in the same string to 16 bits to compare the convenience and storage cost of fixed-width encoding.
context: The two columns are headed "Character" and "Unicode", listing the 7-character string Hello算法 (without spaces) from top to bottom. The table below preserves the 16-bit binary values shown in the figure and adds the corresponding hexadecimal code points converted from binary.
description: In the first five rows, the upper 8 bits of each English character are padded with 00000000 in gray, while the lower 8 bits retain the original code point. The brace on the right reads "One-byte English characters (high bits padded with 0)", and the brace beside the last two rows, "算" and "法", reads "Two-byte Chinese characters".

frames.title: Sixteen-bit view of the code points in Hello算法
frames.explanation: If 1-byte English code points and 2-byte Chinese code points were mixed directly without padding, two consecutive bytes could be misparsed either as a single Chinese character or as two English letters. Zero-padding in the figure makes every character in this example occupy 2 bytes so the stream can be sliced at fixed intervals, at the cost of using twice as much space as ASCII for the five English letters.

tables.caption: Per-character code points of Hello算法

result: This diagram only illustrates 16-bit values for characters within the Basic Multilingual Plane (BMP). Unicode itself defines code points up to U+10FFFF, which require 21 bits; the actual byte length depends on the encoding scheme such as UTF-8 or UTF-16, and not all Unicode characters occupy a fixed 2 bytes.
